title: Edges and triangles present the homotopy category of a quasicategory
statement: Use simplicial sets, quasicategories, standard simplices and degenerate simplices of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. Let $D$ be a quasicategory in a fixed universe. Define $hD$ to have the vertices of $D$ as objects and finite composable words of edges as morphisms, modulo the relations identifying a degenerate edge at $x$ with $1_x$ and identifying the word $(f,g)$ with $h$ whenever a $2$-simplex has edges $f$ on $[0,1]$, $g$ on $[1,2]$ and $h$ on $[0,2]$; composition is concatenation modulo these relations. Write $[f]$ for the morphism represented by an edge $f$. Every morphism $x\to y$ of $hD$ is $[f]$ for an edge $f:x\to y$ of $D$. For any vertices $x,y,z$ and edges $f:x\to y$, $g:y\to z$, $h:x\to z$, the equality $[g]\circ[f]=[h]$ in $hD$ holds if and only if there exists a $2$-simplex of $D$ with exactly these three edges. The assertion includes degenerate edges and empty quasicategories and holds in each input universe.

source.place: Cisinski, Higher Categories and Homotopical Algebra, July 30, 2026, Section 1.6, Lemma 1.6.2, Lemma 1.6.4 and Theorem 1.6.6, printed pp. 21-25 (PDF pp. 36-40). Theorem 1.6.6 identifies the edge-and-triangle presentation tau(D) with the category of homotopy classes of edges; Lemma 1.6.2 realizes composition equations by triangles. Read online 2026-10-17; not archived under literature/. No Stacks tag states this quasicategorical theorem. proof.text: Apply [lem-coef-edge-homotopy-quotient-calculus] to $D$, writing $H=H_L(D)$ and $q(f)$ for its edge classes. The hypotheses are exactly that $D$ fills inner horns. In particular the $2$-horn gives the chosen composite, while the two inner $3$-horns are available for the category laws and triangle criterion in the cited statement. This quotient of single edges is a separate category from the presented $hD$; we construct their comparison below.

source.place: Lines 54-79,203-225,295-311: specialize the 2-truncated edge quotient to D.

proof.text: Map each vertex of the presented $hD$ to the same vertex of $H$, and a word $(f_1,\ldots,f_n)$ to $q(f_n)\circ\cdots\circ q(f_1)$; the empty word goes to the identity. The identity and triangle clauses of [lem-coef-edge-homotopy-quotient-calculus] show that the two kinds of generating relation have equal images. Prepending or appending words preserves these equalities by the category laws in $H$. Hence this map is well defined on the congruence quotient and respects concatenation, giving a functor $F:hD\to H$ with $F([f])=q(f)$.

source.place: Lines 220-225,252,295-311; direct quotient-of-words construction using the cited category.

proof.text: Define $G$ on objects to be the identity and put $G(q(f))=[f]$. If $f\sim_L f'$, its witnessing triangle has boundary $(f,1_y,f')$, so the defining relations of $hD$ give $[f']=[1_y]\circ[f]=[f]$. This proves that $G$ is well defined on each quotient of edges, using the exact relation in [lem-coef-edge-homotopy-quotient-calculus]. Its identity is preserved since $[1_x]=1_x$. For composition choose an inner $2$-horn filler with successive edges $f,g$ and long edge $k$. The cited construction of $H$ makes $q(g)\circ q(f)=q(k)$, and the defining triangle relation in $hD$ makes $[g]\circ[f]=[k]$. Thus $G$ respects composition and is a functor.

source.place: Lines 78-79,213-225,252: quotient descent and verification on a chosen composite triangle; direct argument.

proof.text: For each edge $f$, one has $GF([f])=[f]$ and $FG(q(f))=q(f)$. Every morphism of $hD$ is represented by a finite word, so functoriality proves $GF$ is the identity on morphisms by induction on word length, starting with the empty word. Every morphism of $H$ is an equivalence class of a single edge by its quotient definition in [lem-coef-edge-homotopy-quotient-calculus], so $FG$ is also the identity on all morphisms. Both composites are the identity on objects. For an arbitrary $\alpha:x\to y$ in $hD$, choose an edge representative $f$ of the quotient class $F(\alpha)$; then $\alpha=GF(\alpha)=G(q(f))=[f]$. This proves the first assertion.

source.place: Lines 213,240-245: quotient representatives; direct inverse-functor and word-induction calculation.

proof.text: If $[g]\circ[f]=[h]$ in $hD$, apply $F$ to get $q(g)\circ q(f)=q(h)$ in $H$. The triangle criterion of [lem-coef-edge-homotopy-quotient-calculus] supplies a $2$-simplex whose prescribed short edges are $f,g$ and whose long edge is exactly $h$. Conversely, any such simplex imposes $[g]\circ[f]=[h]$ among the defining relations of $hD$. This proves the second assertion; it does not replace a boundary edge by a merely homotopic edge.

source.place: Lines 295-297: triangle criterion applied after the constructed comparison functor.

proof.text: All the categories and quotients above are formed from the sets of vertices, edges, triangles and finite edge words in the input universe; quotienting those sets preserves that universe. The lemma applies with no distinctness requirement on vertices and no nondegeneracy requirement on edges, so it includes degenerate edges. If $D$ is empty, both categories have no objects and all vertex-indexed assertions are vacuous. The empty word at any existing vertex represents the degenerate identity edge by step 4, including the one-vertex case. Thus no nonemptiness hypothesis or universe enlargement has entered the proof.
